payload.name: Preserve Prior Facts When Updating Memory
payload.description: Apply during CRUD when a new message adds a detail to an existing preference, state, or profile memory, to avoid replacing older supported facts with a narrower statement.
content: During CRUD, before UPDATE or MERGE, compare the new evidence with the stored content. If the new fact is additional rather than contradictory, preserve the old facts and append the new detail instead of overwriting the whole memory.
Use MERGE or an additive UPDATE when the prior facts are still supported by earlier messages; do not rewrite the memory to only the new detail.
Do not mark the memory as a correction or change its kind/start date unless the source message explicitly states the previous fact was wrong or no longer true.

candidates.solves: When later information adds a new detail to an existing memory, the Construction Agent sometimes overwrites the entire memory with the new detail, losing previously supported facts. This skill prevents that by requiring the agent to preserve old facts unless the new evidence explicitly contradicts them.

payload.name: Preserve Distinct Events During Memory Update
payload.description: When updating or merging an event memory with new evidence that describes a different occurrence of the same activity, use this to keep both events separate.
content: During UPDATE or MERGE of an event memory, compare the new evidence's time and ordinal (e.g., 'first', 'regional', 'fourth') with the existing memory. If they describe distinct occurrences, do not overwrite the existing content; keep the original event and add a separate event memory for the new one.

Only update/replace the existing memory when the new evidence clearly refers to the same occurrence. If times or ordinals differ, preserve the original event's who/what/date and record the new event with its own date.
Stop once the original event and the new event are each represented in a memory; do not add unrelated details.

candidates.solves: Prevents losing an earlier event when new evidence describes a different occurrence of the same activity; an UPDATE or MERGE must not overwrite a distinct past event with a newer one.

payload.name: Preserve Prior Facts on Memory Update
payload.description: During CRUD, when updating an existing memory with new or more detailed information, merge new facts while preserving prior facts and dates that remain true.
content: During CRUD, when new information updates an existing memory, do not replace the whole content with a new summary; merge the new facts into the previous content and keep every prior fact that is still true and not contradicted.
Preserve the existing world_start (begin date) unless the new message explicitly revises it; do not reset it to the timestamp of the later message.
If the prior memory records a duration or implied start date derived from an earlier statement, carry that date into the updated version rather than dropping it.
If the new message contradicts one field, keep the newer value, but retain the other previously recorded facts that remain valid.

candidates.solves: Construction agents frequently lose already-recorded facts when a later message updates an existing memory: the whole memory is replaced and time fields are reset, erasing earlier details such as names, counts, or the implied adoption/start year. This skill ensures UPDATE operations merge new information with the prior memory and preserve facts and world_start dates that remain true.

payload.name: Preserve Distinct Prior Plans on Update
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory with a new plan or event, use if the new evidence involves a different activity, date, or companion than the stored memory.
content: During CRUD, before UPDATE or MERGE of an existing memory, compare the new plan's activity, participants, and timing with the stored memory's existing facets.

If the new plan is a different activity or a separate scheduled occurrence (e.g., painting next Saturday vs. kayaking on a later date), do not overwrite the existing memory content; create a new memory for the new plan or merge only the new distinct facets while preserving the old plan and its date.
Treat evidence as contradictory only when it explicitly denies or replaces the exact same planned activity and time; otherwise preserve the prior fact.
Stop after storing the new plan once; do not create near-duplicate memories of the same plan.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes overwrite a previously stored plan or event memory when a later, unrelated plan is mentioned, discarding the original fact. This skill ensures distinct plans with different activities, dates, or participants are kept as separate memories, and prior facts are preserved unless new evidence directly contradicts them.

payload.name: Preserve Existing Facts When Enriching Memories
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory with new details during CRUD, or when building an enrichment candidate during extraction.
content: During CRUD, when an UPDATE or MERGE has update_type 'enrichment', retain all existing explicit facts already stored in the memory (names, counts, dates, locations, etc.) unless the new message directly contradicts them.
Combine the new details with the old content instead of replacing it; only drop a previously stored fact when the latest message explicitly says it changed or was wrong.

During extraction, when drafting a candidate that targets an existing memory, include the existing memory's durable facts along with the newly stated attributes, so the subsequent CRUD update does not lose them.

candidates.solves: Prevents memory updates from silently dropping previously captured facts when new related details are added. For example, when a later message adds breed information about a person's pets, the update should preserve the already-stored pet names rather than replacing them with only the new attributes.

payload.name: Preserve Prior Facts When Enriching Memories
payload.description: Use when updating or merging an existing memory with new messages that add details about the same subject, to ensure previously stored explicit facts are retained.
content: During CRUD (UPDATE/MERGE), compare any proposed new memory content against the existing version it targets before writing.

Retain every explicit fact already stored in the existing memory unless a new message directly contradicts it; add newly stated details as additional facets rather than replacing the old content with a narrower paraphrase.
Stop after consolidating the preserved facts with the new explicit details; do not infer or add unrelated attributes.

candidates.solves: When the Construction Agent enriches an existing memory with new conversation details, it sometimes rewrites the memory as a narrower summary and drops explicit facts stored earlier, making those facts unavailable for later questions. This skill ensures that UPDATE and MERGE operations preserve prior explicit attributes while adding new ones.

payload.name: Verify Event Coverage Before SKIP
payload.description: Use during CRUD decisions before skipping an event candidate as already represented; check whether the existing memory covers the specific event details, not just a related theme.
content: During CRUD, before SKIPping a candidate as already represented, compare against the matched memory's specific facts: subject, action, object, and time. A general trait, impact, or preference statement does not cover a specific event.

If the existing memory only overlaps thematically (e.g., a writing-impact profile vs. a received-letter event), do not SKIP; ADD a new event memory or MERGE only if the event details are already present.
Check the full existing memory content for the event's distinguishing facts; do not assume an enrichment update will later add them, because it may not.

candidates.solves: Construction decisions sometimes skip a correctly extracted event because a related profile or preference memory seems to cover the same theme, losing the specific event and its timing. This guides CRUD to require event-specific facts before skipping.

payload.name: Preserve Distinct Event Facts on Update
payload.description: When updating an existing event memory with new message content, first check whether the new activity/event is the same as the memory's; if it is a distinct past event, keep the original memory and ADD a new one.
content: During CRUD/update, before replacing an existing memory's content or world_start with new event details, verify that the new message describes the same event (same activity, companions, and timeframe).
If the new event differs in activity, companions, or time, do not UPDATE the existing memory; instead ADD a new memory for the new event and leave the original unchanged.
When uncertain, prefer adding a distinct memory over overwriting; multiple past events with the same subject at different times must coexist.

candidates.solves: Prevents construction updates from overwriting an earlier event memory when a later message mentions a different event. The agent should distinguish same-event updates from distinct events and preserve original facts by adding a separate memory.

payload.name: Detail-Level Coverage Check Before Skip
payload.description: When deciding whether to SKIP or MERGE a candidate during construction, check whether the existing memory explicitly contains every distinct fact in the candidate; apply before any SKIP or MERGE.
content: During CRUD decisions, before SKIPping or MERGEing a candidate, verify the target memory explicitly contains every distinct factual detail in the candidate (who, what, when, and any specific artifact or event).
If any detail is missing, do not SKIP or MERGE; add the candidate as a new memory or enrich the existing memory with the missing details.
Do not treat a broader thematic statement (e.g., 'writing brought comfort to others') as covering a specific distinct fact (e.g., 'someone wrote her a letter about her blog post on a hard moment').
Stop after preserving the missing details; do not rewrite or duplicate unrelated existing content.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes discard a correctly extracted event candidate because an existing memory covers the same subject or a related outcome, but the existing memory omits a specific factual detail. This skill prevents loss of answerable facts by requiring a detail-level coverage check before SKIP/MERGE decisions.

payload.name: Preserve Existing Facts When Enriching Memories
payload.description: When updating or enriching an existing memory with additional details from later messages, apply this to keep previously recorded explicit facts that remain true.
content: During UPDATE or MERGE operations that enrich an existing memory, add or integrate the newly stated details into the current content rather than replacing the whole content.
Before rewriting, list the explicit facts already stored; keep every fact that is still true and not contradicted by the new evidence, including concrete outcomes and achievements.
If new details refine the subject (e.g., project focus), update those specifics but do not delete older explicit accomplishments unless the new source explicitly denies or supersedes them.
Stop once the new details are incorporated; do not add unrelated facts or rephrase away the speaker's concrete wording.

candidates.solves: Memory UPDATE operations that enrich an existing record with new details often overwrite the previous content, dropping earlier explicit facts such as achievements or outcomes. This skill teaches the Construction Agent to preserve all still-true explicitly stated facts when appending or integrating new information, preventing later queries from missing evidence-backed claims.

payload.name: Preserve Distinct Events on Update
payload.description: When updating or merging memories during CRUD, if a new message describes a different event than the existing memory, even for the same person, keep both as separate memories instead of overwriting.
content: During CRUD, before applying UPDATE or MERGE to an existing memory, determine whether the incoming evidence describes the same real-world event or a distinct event. Distinct if the event type, time, or occurrence differs (e.g., pregnancy vs marriage announcement).
If the events are distinct, do not overwrite or replace the existing memory. ADD a separate memory for the new event and retain the old one intact.

Only UPDATE/MERGE when the new information truly corrects or extends the same event (e.g., a more precise date or explicit retraction). Do not assume same subject or near timing implies the same event.
After preserving the distinct event, stop; do not create redundant copies of the same new event.

candidates.solves: Prevents loss of previously stored facts when a later message describes a new event related to the same person or partner. Construction agents sometimes overwrite an existing event memory with a different event that shares the same subject or close timing, erasing the original fact.

payload.name: Preserve Existing Explicit Facts During Memory Merge
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory with new evidence, use this to retain all explicit claims from the prior version unless directly contradicted.
content: During CRUD-stage UPDATE/MERGE, compare the existing memory's explicit facts with the new evidence before changing content.

Keep every explicit claim from the existing version (including specific passions, stated beliefs, and named effects) unless the new evidence directly contradicts it; express both old and new facts in the merged memory.

Do not reduce a specific claim to a broader category (for example, do not turn 'passion for fantasy stuff' into 'enjoys fantasy genres') and do not let a newly mentioned theme replace the memory's previous focus.

If the new evidence concerns a different domain, preserve the current memory in place and create or update a separate memory for the new domain; change only fields the new evidence actually contradicts.
Preserve the original world_start unless the new evidence explicitly indicates a new start; stop after merging explicit facts and do not infer additional relationships.

candidates.solves: Later messages often introduce a related but different topic, and an update/merge can rewrite a precise memory into a broader summary, dropping exact claims (like a specific passion or its stated effect) that future questions rely on. This skill makes update/merge operations combine new evidence with the existing memory's explicit facts instead of replacing them.

payload.name: Extract Third-Party Assessments Separately
payload.description: When a message contains both an explicit third-party assessment (e.g., doctor's statement, professional opinion) and a person's attitude or emotion, extract the assessment as its own candidate.
content: During extraction, when a speaker reports an explicit factual statement from another person (e.g., a doctor's assessment, diagnosis, or prognosis) while also expressing an attitude or emotion, create a separate memory candidate for the factual statement, preserving the source and exact content.
Do not let a summarizing state memory about the person's attitude (e.g., 'staying positive') replace or absorb the explicit third-party statement.
During CRUD, if an existing memory contains the attitude but omits the stated assessment, update or merge it to include the assessment rather than leaving the incomplete version.
Stop after capturing the assessment and the attitude; do not add inferred medical details, unstated severity, or speculative outcomes.

candidates.solves: Prevents loss of explicit third-party factual statements (e.g., professional assessments, diagnoses, or prognoses) when extraction focuses on a person's attitude or emotional state, by requiring such statements to be captured as separate memory candidates.

payload.name: Preserve All Explicitly Stated Attributes
payload.description: When a user explicitly lists multiple qualities, reasons, or attributes for liking, admiring, or valuing someone or something during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly enumerates multiple qualities, reasons, or attributes (e.g., 'brave, selfless, down-to-earth attitude'), preserve every listed item in the candidate memory; do not paraphrase away or drop any of them.
Record the attributes closely to the speaker's wording and keep them together in one memory when they describe the same target and relationship.
During CRUD, if a matching memory already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it to add any explicitly stated attributes that are missing, then stop; do not infer or add unmentioned attributes.

candidates.solves: When extracting memories from statements where a user explicitly lists multiple qualities, reasons, or attributes (for example, why they admire a person or character), the extraction step sometimes paraphrases the list into a summary and drops some listed items. This causes later questions about the omitted attributes to fail. The skill ensures every explicitly stated attribute is preserved in the memory so the full set of stated reasons remains retrievable.

payload.name: Preserve All Enumerated Categories in Extraction
payload.description: When a message confirms a question and adds multiple distinct people, groups, or items, during extraction preserve each explicitly named category.
content: During extraction, when a speaker enumerates two or more distinct people, groups, items, or attributes in a single message (including affirmations like 'Definitely!' followed by 'and...'), preserve each distinct category explicitly in the candidate content.

Do not merge or paraphrase the enumeration into a subset or shift modifiers between nouns; e.g., 'old friends and teammates from other tournaments' must yield both 'old friends' and 'teammates from other tournaments', not 'old teammates'.
Stop once every explicitly stated category is captured; do not infer unmentioned categories or expand the list.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates sometimes paraphrase enumerated groups and drop an explicitly stated category, so future questions miss a fact. This skill keeps every distinct category named in an enumeration in the memory candidate.

payload.name: Extract all distinct durable facts per message
payload.description: During extraction, when one message contains two or more independent durable facts about a person, create a separate memory candidate for each fact; do not keep only the most prominent or emotionally salient one.
content: During extraction, if a single message states multiple distinct durable facts about the speaker or another person (e.g., receiving a specific item and experiencing a life event), emit each fact as its own candidate memory instead of combining them or keeping only one.

When one fact is emotionally prominent (e.g., a job loss), do not let it suppress other explicitly stated durable facts in the same message; each explicit durable claim remains eligible for extraction.
Stop after capturing each explicitly stated durable fact; do not infer additional facts or expand beyond the message's content.

candidates.solves: During construction extraction, a single message can contain multiple distinct durable facts, but the extractor sometimes captures only the most salient or emotionally prominent one and drops the others. This skill ensures that every explicitly stated durable fact in a message is emitted as its own candidate memory, so later questions about any of those facts can be answered.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Evaluations with Stated Reasons
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker explicitly praises or evaluates another person's role, abilities, or character and gives specific qualities or reasons for that evaluation.
content: When a speaker explicitly states a positive evaluation of someone (e.g., calling them a perfect mentor, great leader, etc.) and provides specific supporting qualities or reasons, create a durable memory candidate that captures the subject, the evaluation, and the exact stated reasons.
Do not merge these specific reasons only into a generic encouragement or support event; keep them as an explicit part of the evaluation so the reason remains answerable.
Stop after recording the evaluation and the stated reasons; do not infer additional qualities or reasons that were not mentioned.

candidates.solves: When a speaker gives an explicit positive evaluation of another person's role or character (e.g., calling them a perfect mentor) and states specific reasons or qualities, extraction often captures only the generic encouragement and drops the decisive attributes. This makes later questions about why the speaker holds that opinion unanswerable from memory.

payload.name: Extract Multiple Distinct Events from One Message
payload.description: When a message or conversational turn contains multiple explicitly stated events or facts about different people, use this during extraction so each event is captured.
content: During extraction, if a message contains multiple explicit events or facts about different people (or about the same person at different times), create a separate event candidate for each distinct event.
Do not let one salient event cause other explicitly mentioned events in the same message to be omitted; check the whole message and adjacent turns for additional stated facts.
Stop once every explicitly stated distinct event has its own candidate; do not infer events that were not stated.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes captures only one salient event from a message that explicitly contains several, causing other people's actions to be lost. This skill ensures each explicitly stated event is extracted as its own memory candidate.

payload.name: Extract nicknames from direct address
payload.description: During extraction, when a speaker directly addresses someone using a nickname or shortened name, create a relationship memory capturing that nickname.
content: During extraction, identify nicknames or shortened names used in direct address (e.g., 'Hey Jo', 'Thanks Mike'). Create a relationship memory recording that the speaker uses that nickname for the named person, even when the same message also contains an event or other state.
Do not merge the nickname only into an event candidate; make it a separate relationship memory so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only nicknames explicitly stated in direct address; do not infer or generalize beyond the exact term used.

candidates.solves: The Construction Agent sometimes captures only the main event from a message and omits nicknames used in direct address (e.g., 'Hey Jo', 'Thanks Mike'). This causes later questions about what one person calls another to fail, because the nickname was never stored as a durable relationship memory.

payload.name: Preserve All Listed Items in Offer Enumerations
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message lists multiple services, offerings, or coordinated items a person provides; apply before finalizing a candidate.
content: During extraction, when a speaker enumerates two or more services, offerings, or components in a single statement (e.g., 'mentoring and training'), include every listed item in the memory candidate; do not drop one element when paraphrasing.
If a coordinated pair is expressed with 'and' or a list, treat each element as an explicit fact; a summary such as 'mentoring' for 'mentoring and training' loses information.
Stop after capturing all explicitly listed items; do not add services or components the speaker did not mention.

candidates.solves: Extraction from an offer or service description often drops one item when a message lists multiple coordinated services; the resulting memory is incomplete and cannot support later questions about what is offered.
